lines: Nobody tells you why good surfers paddle out where no waves break.
That strip is a rip. It pulls the water back out.
For them it's a free ride to the lineup. Two moves.
One. From the sand, find the gap in the breaking waves.
Two. Paddle out in it, then slide over to the peak.
You get there with fresh arms.
New to surfing? Stay out. Caught in one? Paddle parallel to the beach.
Save it for your next long paddle-out.
Bigger swell, stronger rip. Check it in Surf Tribe.
Tomorrow, why big boards aren't just for beginners.
